question.text: Under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, how must the Investment Manager or Sponsor of a (non-LVF) AIF launch a new scheme with respect to the PPM?

answer.text: File the PPM directly with SEBI at least 7 days prior to launch, without any intermediary.
File the PPM with AMFI and obtain a no-objection certificate before launch.
File the PPM with the custodian who then forwards it to SEBI within 45 days.
File the PPM with SEBI through a SEBI registered Merchant Banker at least 30 days prior to launch of the scheme, along with payment of scheme fee.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the Oct 21, 2021 circular, the Investment Manager/Sponsor must launch AIF schemes after filing the PPM with SEBI, THROUGH A SEBI REGISTERED MERCHANT BANKER, at least 30 days prior to launch, along with payment of scheme fee. (LVFs are exempt — they file directly under an 'intimation' model with a CEO/Compliance Officer undertaking.) The Trap: Direct-to-SEBI filing is only for LVFs. AMFI has no role in AIF PPM filing — AMFI relates to mutual funds. Custodians are back-office service providers, not regulatory filing channels. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the 30-day rule identically. XIX-A Distributor is less likely to ask the merchant-banker mechanics. Manager's Pro-Tip: Lock in your merchant banker early in the scheme-launch calendar: SEBI comments can add 2-4 weeks, and the MB must incorporate those comments BEFORE launch. Plan backwards from your target first-close date.
